title: [bug] layout: subtract-with-overflow panic in label_cells (layout.rs:468) — zero-cell routed paths for same-column band-adjacent edges; spk corpus pipe repro (fan-out repro stale, see notes)
notes:
Rule-of-5 review verification (2026-10-16, HEAD cc20a69): corpus repro CONFIRMED live — spk graph openspec --format dot (337 lines, 333 label= edges) panics at layout.rs:468:27 'attempt to subtract with overflow' in both --as ascii and --as html. GENTLY_TRACE=render.route shows 12 of 333 edges routed cells=0 bends=0 (e.g. e226 ge.layout.t4->ge.layout.positioned) — all same-column, band-adjacent transition->state edges. ROOT CAUSE PINNED: layout/paths.rs multiband_path (east-going branch, ~line 538-549) initializes an empty Vec when gu.0 >= gv.0 and walk_column yields nothing for adjacent rows -> zero-cell path. SPEC BREACH: this violates openspec/specs/ge-layout/spec.md c4/p4 structural clause 'every model edge receives a routed path' (12 unrouted edges). STALE REPRO: the ticket's standalone 4-edge labelled fan-out no longer panics at HEAD — it now errors 'edge 3 turns without changing axis' (fan-out 5/6: 'enters its box through an unsupported side', same class as gently-206); fan placement work (gently-a6g/gently-byq, cc20a69/ac2839f) changed standalone routing. SIMILAR ISSUES (same empty-path class): (1) slot_label_cells layout.rs:491 .expect("slot paths are non-empty") — same false-invariant pattern; (2) renderers panic on empty paths too: render/ascii/polyline.rs:79,130,154 + boxart/polyline.rs:68 .expect("path has a first cell") — guarding label_cells alone just moves the panic downstream; (3) selfloop_path paths.rs:464 returns Vec::new() when no gap row above node; (4) west-going multiband_path paths.rs:535 None => Vec::new() when no gap row at home. FIX SCOPE WIDENED: fix multiband_path/selfloop_path empty branches (emit minimal orthogonal connector or route via reserved gap row), convert silent Vec::new() escapes to an explicit unroutable signal so renderers degrade gracefully (oracle's 'giving up' analog), add corpus pipe regression test (spk graph openspec --format dot | gently --as ascii) satisfying p4, fix the false doc comment at layout.rs:462.
MINIMAL STANDALONE REPRO FOUND (better than corpus): fan-in 5 with labels panics at the same layout.rs:468:27 — digraph { rankdir=LR; s1..s5 -> hub [label="x"] } (edge s4->hub routes cells=0 per GENTLY_TRACE). Unlabelled fan-in 5 does NOT panic: renderers ALREADY guard empty paths gracefully — render/ascii/polyline.rs:74-78 and render/boxart/polyline.rs:63-67 use 'let Some(&first) = ctx.path.first() else { return Err("edge N has an empty path") }' — so the CORRECTION to the earlier similar-issues scan: the polyline .expect()s are POST-guard (unreachable with empty paths); the only truly unguarded empty-path consumer is label_cells itself (runs during layout, before render), and slot_label_cells (layout.rs:491) is the remaining suspect of the same class. MINIMAL FIX: guard label_cells for empty paths (skip label / let renderer's existing guard fire) turns the panic into the same graceful error the unlabelled case gives; the multiband_path routing fix remains the real fix for the ge.layout c4/p4 breach.
FIXED (TDD, this session): (1) label_cells now degrades gently — a labelled edge with an empty path contributes no label cell instead of underflowing (the panic is structurally unreachable now); (2) ROOT CAUSES FIXED in layout/paths.rs: west-going multiband span-hosted fallback (no gap row at 'home' when the endpoints' row spans overlap — was Vec::new()), walk_column no longer backtracks through the dodge column when two stacked nodes sit one free row apart (was a 180° reversal the renderer rejected), walk closes to the face row through the dodge column when the terminal row is blocked (stacked multi-row node fills the walked column), resolve_band's span-ride now honours reserved gap rows (riding bands sat grid-adjacent, starving vertical walks of their cell), east-going run truncates at occupied cells and connects via a face-adjacent approach run (sibling targets stacked at the source's band row, and run rows inside grown targets' spans), straight-overlap rides the actual overlap row (gv's row when gv rides in gu's span — fan-out stack); (3) render/ascii/polyline.rs entry_dir gained the span WEST-side branch (mirror of the east-side rule) so west-ring attachments on continuation rows classify. VERIFIED: new regression tests p4_fanin5_labelled_star_routes_and_renders + p4_fanin8_star_routes_and_renders (red->green); full suite 219 green; just oracle-verify byte-pin green; just clippy/lint/gates green; ah check clean; spk graph openspec --format dot (337 edges, 333 labelled) renders in BOTH --as ascii and --as html; fan-in 5/8/16 labelled and unlabelled render. Spec ge.layout c4/p4 breach resolved — every corpus edge now receives a routed path.

title: Layout: edges into a shared endpoint jump over occupied cells — render rejects non-adjacent path cells
description:
## Repro

Any star graph with two or more edges converging on one node, regardless of
labels, `rankdir`, or input format:

    digraph g {
      rankdir=LR;
      "n1" -> "hub";
      "n2" -> "hub";
      "n3" -> "hub";
      "n4" -> "hub";
    }

Observed (driving gently-core directly: parse::dot → layout::layout →
render::ascii::render):

    render error: edge 2 path cells (2, 3) -> (2, 1) are not orthogonally adjacent

The failing edge's path skips a cell (column gap of 2) — the router jumps over
occupied cells and the renderer's orthogonal-adjacency check rejects it. Fails
identically with and without edge labels and with/without `rankdir=LR`; the
jump offset scales with graph width (`(2, 7) -> (2, 5)` at n=12).

Also fails when parsed from Graph::Easy text (`[ n1 ] -> [ hub ]` star), so this
is layout-side, not dot-parser-side.

## Impact

Blocks all realistic specodelic graph views: `spk graph --view wiring` (16 files
→ `errors` hub) and the corpus-wide dot both fail. Simple chains/diamonds render
fine. This is the second gap blocking the specodelic↔gently integration
(companion issue: CLI DOT wiring).

## Acceptance

- A star graph (both DOT and Graph::Easy text inputs) lays out and renders to
  ASCII without error
- Differential check against the pinned oracle's rendering of the same star
  (ge.oracle) — upstream Graph::Easy routes converging edges with jump-over
  cells
- Perf budgets in ge.perf still hold
design: Likely the path router marks the shared endpoint's occupied cells as pass-through or under-routes: the generated path contains a 2-column jump (e.g. (2,3) -> (2,1)) that render/ascii's adjacency check rejects. Fix in layout (emit adjacency-respecting paths or flag jump-over cells the renderer accepts), not by loosening the renderer check.
notes: Companion: gently-cij (CLI DOT wiring) — both must land before the spk-graph pipe integration demo.
close_reason: Duplicate of gently-4ga — same 'path cells not orthogonally adjacent' defect in layout/paths.rs (fan-out via comma-chains, fan-in via star graphs; one root cause). Repro evidence and cross-repo impact notes transferred to gently-4ga.

title: Wire the DOT parser into the CLI input path
description:
## Problem

`specs/cli.md` states the CLI wires [[ge.text_parser]] and [[ge.dot_parser]], but
`crates/gently-cli/src/pipeline.rs:141` only calls `parse::text`. Feeding a DOT
file fails with a *text*-parser error:

    $ gently --as ascii graph.dot
    gently: parse error, line 1: unknown class 'digraph'
    -> Run: gently doctor

The DOT parser exists and is spec'd (`specs/ge-dot_parser.md`, `parse::dot::parse`
in `crates/gently-core/src/parse/dot/mod.rs`) — it is just unreachable from the CLI.

## Motivation (cross-repo)

This is the first of two gaps blocking the specodelic↔gently integration:
`spk graph <corpus> --format dot` emits DOT with a documented visual grammar and
rendering is external by design (specodelic graph spec decision D8: "pipe into
`dot -Tsvg`, `graph-easy`, …"). With DOT parsing wired, the pipeline becomes:

    spk graph openspec/specs --format dot | gently --as ascii

Integration must stay process-boundary (specodelic is Apache-2.0, gently is
GPL-2.0-or-later — no crate dependency possible).

## Acceptance

- A DOT input parses through the CLI and renders via `--as ascii|html|txt|graphviz`
- Graph::Easy-text input continues to parse unchanged
- The choice mechanism (auto-detect vs explicit flag) is spec'd in cli.md and
  differentially tested against the pinned oracle where it has an opinion
design: Add parser selection to the CLI input path (pipeline.rs). Either auto-detect a leading digraph/graph header or add an upstream-compatible input-format flag; specs/cli.md c-row for input already claims the CLI wires [[ge.dot_parser]], so this closes a conformance gap rather than adding a new capability.

Companion: gently-6hh (layout star bug) — both must land before the spk-graph pipe integration demo.
CORRECTION (issue-review 2026-10-13): companion ticket is now gently-4ga (fan/fan-in layout defect, absorbs the closed gently-6hh). Unblocks the spk-graph | gently pipe demo when both land. Also note gently-fb1 (dot_parser divergence) may surface during differential testing here — related, not a blocker.

title: Mine internet for Graph::Easy examples, edge cases, and known hard cases
description:
## Problem

Human-facing documentation is a single 22-line README with zero examples. The implementation shipped (parse → model → layout → 5 renderers → CLI, byte-compat with the pinned Perl oracle), but a new user cannot see what gently does without reading specs/. Meanwhile the internet contains decades of Graph::Easy material — upstream POD, the Graph::Easy::Manual book, the bloodgate.com site, CPAN scripts, GitHub issue reports, and community Q&A — that documents exactly the examples, edge cases, and known-hard-cases our corpus should cover.

## Goal

Mine those sources into (a) a human-facing examples/docs surface (README + examples/ dir) and (b) corpus fixtures / repro probes for any example or edge case that the current corpus does not already pin. Every mined example must be byte-verified against the pinned oracle (per ge.oracle c7 tier rules) before becoming a fixture or doc example.

## Sources to mine

1. Upstream POD: Graph::Easy, Graph::Easy::Parser, Graph::Easy::Manual (the Manual is a full book — tutorials, FAQ, cookbook)
2. bloodgate.com/perl/graph/ pages (tutorial, examples gallery, ASCII/boxart demos)
3. CPAN scripts + POD synopses across the Graph::Easy ecosystem
4. GitHub issues on ironcamel/Graph-Easy (bug reports = known hard cases)
5. Stack Overflow / PerlMonks / Reddit / blog posts using graph-easy

## Output shape

- examples/ dir with runnable, oracle-verified examples organized by capability
- README examples section (cut-down Diátaxis: quickstart how-to)
- New corpus fixtures or probes entries for uncovered edge cases, filed as follow-up beads
- Known-hard-cases doc page (what diverges from oracle, per byte-compat scope decision 2026-10-09)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each source class mined and findings recorded
- [ ] Every doc example oracle-verified
- [ ] Uncovered cases filed as beads with repro evidence

title: upstream defect (recorded, not filed): Graph::Easy v0.69 as_txt omits a node connected only via a group-endpoint edge (as_ascii renders it)
description:
Recorded upstream defect — DECIDED NOT TO FILE upstream (user, 2026-10-14);
tracked here in beads instead of shlomif/perl-graph-easy.

## Repro (pinned oracle: Graph::Easy v0.69 @ ededa3d787ad89ac532c578c06390e8a7b270499)

```perl
use Graph::Easy::Parser;
my $g = Graph::Easy::Parser->new->from_text("( [ Bonn ] ) -> [ Berlin ]\n");
print $g->as_txt();   # prints only the "( [ Bonn ] )" group block — Berlin is gone
print $g->as_ascii(); # renders BOTH boxes (Bonn, Berlin) — no edge, no group border
```

Also emits: `Warning: Layouter could only place 2 nodes/0 edges out of 2/1 - giving up.`
Byte-identical under `PERL_HASH_SEED=0` and `PERL_HASH_SEED=1` (deterministic).
Recorded: `tests/repro/claims/pod-anon-group.observed` (serves gently-58m).

## Mechanism

The group-end handler makes the closed group the node stack, so the edge
links the GROUP to Berlin. `as_txt`'s declaration pass then never reaches
Berlin as a plain node (its only edge-predecessor is the group); `as_ascii`
takes a different path and still renders it.

## Expected

`as_txt` should list `[ Berlin ]` as an isolated node, consistent with
`as_ascii`. Upstream is self-inconsistent between the two renderers.

## Context

- Adjudicated under the decision-trace E4 pre-registered (b)-checklist
  (gently-btf): items 1, 2, 4, 5 verified; item 3 (upstream issue filed)
  replaced by this beads ticket per user decision — no external post.
- gently's behavior (group block + `[ Berlin ]` listed; dashed border in
  ascii) is renderable and deterministic under ge.layout c1.
- The opening checklist verdict: class (b) — oracle defect, gently
  is right(er) — pending this ticket's existence as the item-3 evidence.

title: spec-drift-gate: failure message misleads when the mirror is fresh-but-unstaged (deployed-mirror commits stall mid-slice)
description:
The pre-commit spec-drift-gate hook (lefthook.yml) regenerates openspec/specs/ via tools/deploy_specs.py and then fails on `git diff --exit-code -- openspec/specs/` — a worktree-vs-INDEX comparison. Two UX problems surfaced in the gently-awd ascii span slice (2026-10-14):

1. MISLEADING FAILURE: after amending the corpus spec AND redeploying, the mirror is FRESH but unstaged — the hook still fails with 'drift: openspec/specs/ is stale — corpus changed without redeploy', which is false (the redeploy happened; the deploy output was just never git-added). The message diagnoses the wrong cause and offers no fix.

2. MID-SLICE COMMIT STALL: the documented protocol is 'deploy the spec mirror only in the same commit as the corpus change'. But when the corpus change is committed FIRST (the TDD RED commit) and the mirror is deployed later in the worktree, EVERY intermediate commit then walks through the drift gate: the hook appears to stall/abort at spec-drift-gate (lefthook frame marker) and git commit exits without creating the commit, leaving the feat staged but uncommitted. The remedy discovered by trial — stage specs/ + openspec/ + specodelic/ INTO the same commit as the feat — is exactly the protocol, but nothing in the failure output says so; it cost a debugging cycle.

SUGGESTED FIX (either or both):
- Detect the fresh-but-unstaged case: after redeploy, compare HEAD:openspec/specs/ to the WORKTREE; if identical, the mirror is current — emit 'drift: deployed mirror is current but unstaged — git add openspec/ + specs/ (+ specodelic/) into this commit' and exit 1 with that message instead of 'stale'.
- Only treat drift as stale when the worktree mirror actually differs from a fresh regeneration AND from the index.

Evidence: session 2026-10-14 (gently-awd), commits cf8d30c (RED, passed — mirror untouched), then the aborted feat commit (staged files left, gate abort at spec-drift-gate), then 8a0d56b succeeded once specs/openspec/specodelic were staged in. Notes mirrored in turu branch recall and bd gently-awd notes.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A fresh-but-unstaged mirror produces the 'current but unstaged — git add ...' message, not 'stale'. 2. A genuinely stale mirror still fails with the redeploy instruction. 3. A commit with specs/+openspec/ staged together passes the gate unchanged.
